# AMB005 amb-overcatch

An ambient class or a root catch-all is a source in a waypoint outcome map.

## What it does

A waypoint mapping `SOURCE => variant;` whose source is one of the ambient classes (`exhausted`, `defect`, `interrupted`, `killed`) or a language root catch-all (`Throwable`, `BaseException`, `recover`) is flagged at the source. The explicit `_` arm is not flagged. Which concrete exception types a bare `Exception` covers needs the adapter and is not judged here.

## Why it matters

Mapping a defect or resource exhaustion to a domain outcome hides bugs as ordinary results, and a catch-all can abort a cluster on a domain error.

## Remedy

Map only the specific domain errors and leave ambient faults to the ambient policy; use `_` for an explicit other arm.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

system s {
  ambient escalate { verified_by "tests/a.py"; }
  actor u : human;
  step u.go : { ok, bad };

  scenario t {
    u.go => {
      ok => end ok;
      bad => end err(bad);
    }
  }

  impl u.go for t {
    chain {
      call c = "a.py::c" {
        defect => bad;
        verified_by "tests/a.py";
      }
    }
  }
}
```
